describes: Acrylic house paint, beside alkyd from the 1960s: a flexible, open film that chalks a little and seldom peels.

notes.chalk: Raised in round 3: a coat a few years up must read older than a new one (the strict review); judged by look.
notes.peel: toWood: the share of what is lost that goes to the wood rather than to the coat under (it blisters off the wood where water is trapped behind it); judged by look. The onset is the open wall's; where water works in (paint.json, weather) it comes two to three times sooner.
notes.all: No source dated or measured it for this town; the values are an assumption judged by look, kept apart so a source can replace them.
notes.water: Its water profile as the town's (Shaders/Water.hlsl, Overstory.World.WaterPack): how much it darkens wet, how glossy its wet film, how long it holds water, how readily run-off stains it. An open film: sheds water, a soft sheen. Judged by look.
